from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The 2D Area Intuition", 
                          ["Determinants represent the area of a parallelogram.", 
                           "Scaling a vector scales the parallelogram area linearly.", 
                           "Determinants track how space is scaled globally."])
        
        # Define objects
        parallelogram = Polygon([0, 0, 0], [3, 0, 0], [4, 2, 0], [1, 2, 0], color=WHITE)

        label_b = MathTex("b", color="#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, "C3")
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(area_fill, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(area_fill))
        
        # Position labels
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(label_h, "C4")
        self.play(Write(label_b), Write(label_h))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(area_fill))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(ThreeDScene, TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Cross Product", [
            "Move to 3D with two distinct vectors.",
            "The cross product produces a perpendicular vector.",
            "Its magnitude is the parallelogram's surface area."
        ])
        
        # Initialize 3D space
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=-45 * DEGREES)
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1], z_range=[-3, 3, 1])
        self.add(axes)

        # Assets
        u = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.array([1, 2, 0]), color=WHITE)
        v = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.array([2, -0.5, 1]), color=WHITE)
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            np.array([0, 0, 0]),
            np.array([1, 2, 0]),
            np.array([3, 1.5, 1]),
            np.array([2, -0.5, 1]),
            color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(u), FadeIn(v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Cross product vector
        cross_vec = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.array([0.5, -0.5, 2.5]), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(cross_vec))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The scalar triple product computes volume.",
            "Cross products relate to volumetric transformations.",
            "It scales the volume of the unit cube.",
            "Linear transformations squash or stretch space volume.",
            "Cross products describe face normals in 3D."
        ]

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Application: The Normal Vector", [
            "Surface normals are vital for 3D lighting.",
            "Cross products compute these normals efficiently.",
            "Light reflection depends on surface orientation.",
            "Lighting calculations use normals for pixel color.",
            "Physics simulations rely on these geometric tools."
        ])

        # Objects
        # Create vectors and plane for 3D space
        # Using 3D setup as per instruction [B021]
        v1 = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.array([1, 0, 0.5]), color="#FFFFFF")
        v2 = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.array([0, 1, 0.5]), color="#FFFFFF")
        plane = Surface(
            lambda u, v: u * np.array([1, 0, 0.5]) + v * np.array([0, 1, 0.5]),
            u_range=[-1, 1], v_range=[-1, 1],
            color="#555555"
        ).set_opacity(0.3)
        normal = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.cross([1, 0, 0.5], [0, 1, 0.5]), color="#FF00FF")
        normal_label = MathTex(r"\vec{n}", color="#FF00FF")

        # Position elements on grid using 3D camera logic implicitly via scene
        # Since I am in 3D but constrained to 6x6 grid, I will render them centrally
        # [B034] Avoid C3, D3 origin centers. Using B2, B4 for objects
        group = VGroup(v1, v2, plane, normal)
        self.place_at_grid(group, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Write(v1), Write(v2), Create(plane))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), Write(normal))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # [B038] explicitly label the normal variable
        self.place_at_grid(normal_label, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), Write(normal_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Magnitude is area, direction is normal.", "Cross product bridges geometry and algebra.", "It is central to modern 3D rendering."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The 'Flow' of Cross Products", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        parallelogram = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2, RIGHT*2+UP*1.5, UP*1.5, color=WHITE)

outline.topic: The Geometric Intuition of Cross Products and Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The 2D Area Intuition
sections.content: Briefly define the 2D determinant as the signed area of a parallelogram spanned by two vectors. Establish that scaling vectors changes the area proportionally.
sections.example: Imagine two 'vector sticks' on a table forming a shadow. If you stretch one stick, the shadow area grows linearly.

sections.title: Defining the Cross Product via the Parallelogram
sections.content: Transition to 3D space. Define the cross product as a vector whose magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram formed by two vectors, and whose direction is perpendicular (Right-Hand Rule).
sections.example: Visualize a robotic arm's two joints; the cross product magnitude represents the 'swept area' the arm covers during a swing.

sections.title: The Linear Transformation Link: Determinants in 3D
sections.content: Explain that the cross product is inherently linked to the 3D determinant (the scalar triple product). It measures how a linear transformation changes the volume of a unit cube.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'cube of jelly' being squashed or stretched by a matrix; the cross product helps calculate the surface normal of the cube's faces.

sections.title: Geometric Application: The Normal Vector
sections.content: Demonstrate why the cross product is the tool of choice for finding surface normals—critical for lighting in computer graphics and physics simulations.
sections.example: A 3D character (e.g., a cyber-fox) standing in a game engine; the cross product calculates the surface normal of its fur triangles to determine how light reflects off them.

sections.title: Summary: The 'Flow' of Cross Products
sections.content: Recap: Cross product = Magnitude (Area) + Direction (Normal). It is the bridge between vector geometry and the volumetric perspective of linear algebra.
sections.example: A quick visual montage: From two lines forming a plane, to the orthogonal vector shooting out, to the lighting engine calculating the final pixel color.
